newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower on rains, weak exports.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower on rains, weak exports.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter closed lower on improving crop prospects in Kansas and lower-than-expected weekly U.S. export inspections.
"The rains in Kansas (over the holiday weekend) led to lower prices at the opening and we fell to the day's lows when the export news came out," a floor trader said.
Crops in northwest Kansas received at least 0.50 inch of rain over the three-day weekend, providing a major boost as they start to head out, meteorologists said.
Cool temperatures continued to improve the outlook for freeze-damaged crops in southern Kansas, they added.
Below-normal temperatures have delayed maturity and given tillers more chances to recover, meteorologists said.

"I don't think they could have looked for a much better weather pattern than they have seen since the freeze with the exception of the dryness in northwestern Kansas," said Mike Palmerino, senior agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Weekly export data were also bearish, dealers said.
USDA said for the week ended May 22, U.S. wheat inspected for export totaled 6.960 million bushels, below expectations for 10 million to 14 million bushels.
Featured net sellers included FIMAT, Cargill Investor Services and E.D. and F. Man International while Prudential Securities and Rosenthal Collins Group were noted buyers.
July closed 11-1/2 cents lower at $3.89 per bushel, with other months down 10-1/4 cents to up one cent.
